hero.title: Files cross as descriptors.
hero.lede: A chat image reaches a provider as a read-only file handle over the broker socket. The broker keeps no copy, the model never sees the bytes, and every ceiling counts decoded bytes.

summary: Move images through the capability boundary without copying them into JSON, and bound what a provider can upload or attach. Permission still lives in the broker.

highlights.title: The guest gets a handle, never a path.
highlights.body: chat-asset:3 in a proposal becomes a read-only descriptor passed with the request. The Wasm guest reads it positionally in 64 KiB pieces and never holds the fd. Outputs come back the same way: attached, unlinked, and admitted by the gateway without a copy.
points: attach retains; asset send delivers, four per turn
5 files and 40 MiB decoded per invocation
A trap, denial, or timeout admits no asset effect

highlights.title: Uploads are exact-length and hashed as they leave.
highlights.body: A provider composes a body from literal parts and asset parts; the host re-encodes on the fly, declares Content-Length, and records the SHA-256 of what it sent. Every asset occurrence is charged before dispatch, repeats included.
points: maxHttpRequestBytes covers method, URL, headers, and literals
Asset bytes count against the 40 MiB decoded ceiling
A response with Content-Encoding is refused

highlights.title: Old attachment keys refuse to load.
highlights.body: providerAttachments and chatAssetInputs no longer parse, even empty. References resolve automatically; delivery needs an asset.send grant. Asset-producing providers must be rebuilt on dekopon:asset; the old base64 result envelope is refused after the call.
points: Core, providers, and chart land in one order
Grant asset.send to the asset command provider only
References and queued sends don’t survive restart

path.title: Six hops, zero copies.
path.body: The descriptor rides the sendmsg that carries the frame’s first byte, so file and request arrive together.
path.ariaLabel: One 8 MiB chat image crossing to a provider and back

changes.title: The input attribute stops at 4096 bytes.
changes.body: input.bytes carries the uncut length; recording it whole cost 96.0 MiB of allocator peak for one 8 MiB image.

changes.title: Request bodies are built once, compact, with Content-Length.
changes.body: One 8 MiB image cost 33.8 MB per step before; frames are allocated at the size they carry.

changes.title: The broker gets a disk-backed asset volume.
changes.body: The volume is 320Mi and mounts in the broker container only, so the gateway can’t see it. Write the assets: block into the inline broker config yourself.

detailsIntro: The chart provisions the volume; your inline broker config names it. A broker without an assets section still reads handles but refuses allocate and stream.

telemetry.title: authority moved to the gateway or model
telemetry.body: The model still asks and the broker still authorizes. A passed descriptor grants nothing; attach, remove, and send are three separate grants.
telemetry.note: A compromised gateway can vouch for any subject in its attestor lane. This release does not harden that boundary.

packages.name: Homebrew
packages.body: The generated formula installs both executables from the attested release archives.

packages.name: crates.io
packages.body: Every public crate is published at the application version. Downstream builds do not inherit the workspace-only tracing-core patch used by the release archives and image.

packages.name: Container
packages.body: The Debian 13 distroless image carries both executables from the release archives and the pinned provider components.

installIntro: Install both daemons from the attested archives, or use one of the packages below. The Helm chart has its own publication schedule.
